What the numbers say

For the session of Wednesday, October 28, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (26 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as mixed. SPY is above its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is sideways and realised volatility is in the calm band.

10 of 26 tickers (38%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 18 of 25 (72%) above their 200-day average. That sits between the model's 30% and 55% breadth thresholds, so breadth alone decides nothing here. On the day 12 rose and 14 fell; the median move was −0.25%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Technology had the strongest average move at +0.76% and Consumer Discretionary the weakest at −0.53%, a spread of 1.29 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 1.05 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

1 ticker has a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (NFLX), and none is at or above 70. An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-10-27), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 42% to 38%, and the regime reading changed from neutral to mixed.
